title.narrative: Response to floods affected communities in Borno State, Nigeria

description.narrative: On Tuesday, 10 September 2024, severe flash floods inundated 40 per cent of Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC), Jere and Konduga Local Government Areas (LGAs) in Borno State, Northeast Nigeria. Some 300,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) sought shelter in 29 camps, 60 per cent of which are schools. Some 40 per cent of health facilities that also offer nutrition services have been damaged by the floods. Furthermore, the floods have caused significant damage to critical infrastructure, including the collapse of one and damage of another major bridge in Maiduguri, limiting access to essential services. The health sector has been critically affected, with approximately 40 per cent of inpatient beds and nutrition facilities damaged, leading to a significant reduction in healthcare capacity. The state’s cold store, responsible for preserving vaccines, was also flooded, resulting in the loss of 1.1 million vaccine doses, further jeopardizing health services. Overcrowded camps, inadequate sanitation, and the destruction of health infrastructure have elevated the risk of disease outbreaks, especially cholera, measles, and malaria. Measles cases were already reported across 25 of Borno’s 27 local government areas (LGAs) earlier this year, with over 5,000 suspected cases.With CERF’s Rapid Response funding, UNICEF's response will mitigate the impact of floods and the risk of waterborne diseases for nearly 30,000 people in need, including vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, children under the age of 5, and people with disabilities. The health response will focus on emergency primary health care services to address waterborne and vaccine-preventable childhood diseases by ensuring continued access to health services by rehabilitating health facilities and improving health-seeking behaviours through community engagement.The WASH response will comprise the distribution of critical WASH supplies, the provision of essential services, including water system rehabilitation and toilet construction, environmental sanitation and conducting hygiene promotion campaigns. Child Protection interventions will respond to protection concerns in three key areas: the provision of psychosocial support for flood-affected children, the prevention of family separation and the reunification of separated and unaccompanied children, as well as the strengthening of community-based protection systems related to GBV.
